name: Gaja Alternative Asset Management Ltd
title: Gaja Alternative Asset Management Ltd - 544885 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Asset manager with 100% fee and performance economics; Q1 FY27 PAT up 35% to INR27.2 crore, but performance income (INR29.7 crore) is lumpy and management declined to give forward guidance.

triggers.label: No forward guidance policy
triggers.quote: as a policy, we have chosen not to issue future guidance

triggers.label: Carry booked on realised basis, lumpy
triggers.quote: we do not book carried interest on an accrual basis. We book carried interest on a realized basis.

triggers.label: Fund V and Eastgate commitments sought
triggers.quote: We are seeking commitments of INR2,500 crores over a closed-ended term of 10 years.

triggers.label: Fund IV 81% deployed post-quarter
triggers.quote: we were 75% deployed as on June. Since then, we've made another call, which has taken the deployment to 81%.

red_flags.label: Performance income mostly sponsor gains on NAV marks
red_flags.quote: the performance income of the fund consists of two portions. One, the carried fee or carried income, and second is income from sponsor gains.

red_flags.label: Refuses forward guidance and fund timelines
red_flags.quote: we will not be issuing future guidance

red_flags.label: Fund III gross IRR ~9% questioned on carry
red_flags.quote: It's too early to say because, generally, we carry valuations on a conservative basis.

evasions.topic: Future performance / carry timing from Fund III
evasions.quote: that will be making a futuristic statement, which we are not authorized to make.
we cannot issue future guidance while answering your questions.
Which variation are you referring to?

summary.headline: Gaja AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR27.2 crores; total income up 26% to INR51.8 crores.
summary.overview: First quarterly call as a listed company. Total income rose 26% YoY to INR51.8 crores and PAT rose 35% to INR27.2 crores, with LTM PAT at INR89.1 crores (+38%). Performance income of INR29.7 crores (+17% YoY) drove most of the income, while management fee income of about INR16 crores grew 7%. Cost-to-income improved to 38.4% from 42.3%. Management repeatedly declined to give forward guidance on carry, fund deployment or fundraising timelines.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: About INR16 crores in Q1 FY27, up 7% YoY. Management fee is charged on initial committed capital of Funds III and IV, roughly INR3,200 crores, not on AUM.

segments.name: Performance income
segments.commentary: INR29.7 crores in Q1 FY27, up 17% YoY; LTM INR92.2 crores (INR72 crores sponsor gains and INR20 crores carry per the LTM split given on the call). Carry is booked on a realised basis only. Q1 carry of INR13 crores came from Fund II.

guidance_outlook: Management has a stated policy of not giving future guidance on carry, fund wind-up, deployment or fundraising timelines.
Fund V (flagship) targets INR2,500 crores over a 10-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received. Management said the size may increase a bit.
Eastgate (secondaries) targets INR1,500 crores over a 5-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received.
Historical trendlines cited: profit about 35% CAGR (Mar-24 to Mar-26) and total income about 24% a year. Not presented as guidance.
Dividend of INR0.75 per share (15%); payout ratio raised to 12.5% from about 10%.
PW (PricewaterhouseCoopers) to be appointed statutory auditor, replacing the previous auditor.
capex_capacity: Fund V (flagship): seeking INR2,500 crores over a 10-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received; management said size may increase a bit; targets 10-12 investments; enterprise values up to INR2,000 crores with scale potential to INR10,000 crores.
Eastgate (secondaries): seeking INR1,500 crores over a 5-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received; provides liquidity to Indian PE/VC managers via portfolio stake acquisitions.
Fund IV: closed 2023 at INR1,775 crores across 7 investments; 75% deployed at 30 June 2026, rising to 81% after one further call; gross IRR 29%, gross MOIC 1.8x.
Fee-paying initial committed capital of Funds III and IV is roughly INR3,200 crores; management said fee income does not grow with NAV.
Management said the two new funds (Fund V and Eastgate) are proposed for launch in FY26-27 and declined to give timelines for wind-up, deployment or first close.
demand_pricing: Fund IV (closed 2023, INR1,775 crores, 7 investments): 75% deployed at 30 June 2026, now 81% after one more investment; gross IRR 29%, gross MOIC 1.8x.
Fund III gross IRR cited at about 9% (analyst figure, from CRISIL cohort data); management says it already earns sponsor gains from Fund III.
Sponsor commitment across funds about INR589 crores, 7.1% of fund size.
Investor base: 298 LPs in existing funds; about 900 investors across India and 20+ countries; little reliance on distributors.
Hurdle rates: 10% for rupee investors, 8% for dollar investors; European (whole-fund) waterfall with full catch-up.

qa_highlights.question: Fund IV dry powder and number of targeted investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 10-12 investments per fund; seven made in Fund IV by June 2026, deployment at 75% rising to 81% since. Fund V will also target 10-12 investments.

qa_highlights.question: Share of carry vs fee income and whether pure fee income will grow faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said performance income becomes more predictable as firms mature, and that fee income does not grow with NAV. Q1 split was about INR16 crores fee and INR30 crores performance; LTM is the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of performance income into carry and sponsor gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: INR13 crores carry from Fund II and INR17 crores sponsor gains from Funds III and IV, total INR29.7 crores. LTM performance income INR92.2 crores (INR72 crores sponsor gains, INR20 crores carry). Carry is booked on realised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Fund III carry given low gross IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to say; NAVs are carried conservatively and it expects Fund III performance income trends to continue, with sponsor gains already flowing.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 to Q1 jump of about 594% in carry fee; is it realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 FY26 weakness to low markets and multiple re-rating in March 2026. The Q1 jump reflects fair value gains from the recovery in markets through June, not realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to AI deals such as Fractal and Sarvam and entry valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to discuss underlying fund investments in detail. Said both are mature growth-stage deals, not venture; sector exposure capped at 20-25% of fund capital.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost rise from Q4 to Q1 (INR6.7 crores to INR10.3 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 has seasonal bonus payouts; YoY, Q1 employee costs are in the same range of INR10-plus crores.

qa_highlights.question: Market value of portfolio and LP share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no single portfolio; valuations are done quarterly under SEBI rules and the same valuations are used for the company's holdings.

qa_highlights.question: Fund III and Fund V, Eastgate timelines and first closes?
qa_highlights.answer: Declined to give future guidance on wind-up, deployment or fundraising timing.

risks_watch: Performance income is lumpy quarter to quarter (Q4 FY26 carry sharply lower, Q1 FY27 up about 594% QoQ); management asks investors to judge on LTM.
Fund III gross IRR of about 9% is well below the 10% rupee hurdle and carry depends on returning capital plus hurdle; no carry guidance given.
Carry is booked only on realisations, so timing of fund exits will drive reported earnings.
Fund IV valuation and AI-sector exposure (Fractal, Sarvam) questioned by analysts; management declined detailed disclosure.
Auditor change to PW and fundraising for Fund V (INR2,500 crores) and Eastgate (INR1,500 crores) are pending milestones.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the franchise and historical numbers, but evasive on forward-looking items. Management repeatedly declined guidance on carry, deployment, fund-raise timing and Fund III outcome, citing board and adviser advice. Explanations of quarterly variance leaned on LTM framing.

financial_highlights.value: INR29.7 crores (carry INR13 crores from Fund II; sponsor gains INR17 crores from Fund III and IV)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR534 crores a year earlier

key_quotes: So, typically from a fund, we invest in 10 to 12 companies, say 10 companies.
We currently have two funds on the drawing board.
So, as a policy, we have chosen not to issue future guidance.
The carried interest line, as you've rightly said, comes from Fund II. The sponsor gain line comes from Fund III and Fund IV.
And we do not book carried interest on an accrual basis. We book carried interest on a realized basis.

growth.why: Management declined forward guidance on carry, deployment or fundraising timelines, citing a no-guidance policy; the only growth backing is two proposed new funds (Fund V at INR2,500 crores and Eastgate at INR1,500 crores, both SEBI-approved, launch proposed in FY26-27) with no firm timelines, while the Q1 total income rose 26% and PAT 35% YoY on performance income and cost control.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Cost-to-income improved to 38.4% from 42.3% YoY and total expenses rose only 14% vs total income +26%, but performance income is lumpy and carry is booked only on realisations, so margins depend on fund exits.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY26-27 (proposed launch of Fund V and Eastgate, no firm tim
rows.why: Fund V (INR2,500 crores) and Eastgate (INR1,500 crores) have SEBI approval and launch is proposed for FY26-27, but management declined timelines for first close or deployment.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Fee income grew only 7% YoY to about INR16 crores as it is charged on initial committed capital (~INR3,200 crores) rather than AUM, so volume growth hinges on the two new funds launching; Fund IV is 81% deployed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Asset-light fund manager with no physical capacity; the relevant analogue is fund launches, which are already under way via SEBI-approved Fund V and Eastgate.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management has a stated no-guidance policy and declined forward views on carry, deployment and fundraising; Q1 PAT +35% is driven by lumpy fair-value gains and Fund III IRR of about 9% is below the 10% hurdle.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Performance income is lumpy (Q4 FY26 carry sharply lower, Q1 FY27 up about 594% QoQ), carry is realisation-based, and Fund III gross IRR of about 9% is below the 10% rupee hurdle, so a weak exit quarter could cut reported earnings.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said Fund V (INR2,500 crores, 10-12 investments) and Eastgate (INR1,500 crores, 5-year term) are proposed for launch in FY26-27 with SEBI approval already received, though no first-close timing was given.

rows.label: Fund IV deployment rising toward full
rows.why: Fund IV is 81% deployed after one more investment (75% at 30 June 2026) across 7 investments of a INR1,775 crore fund, so remaining dry powder is limited and new deal flow is needed.

rows.label: Auditor change to PwC and dividend payout raise
rows.why: PW is to be appointed statutory auditor and the dividend was raised to INR0.75 per share with payout moving to 12.5% from about 10%.

rows.label: Fund III carry outlook uncertain
rows.why: Fund III gross IRR of about 9% (analyst figure) is below the 10% rupee hurdle, so carry from Fund III is doubtful even though sponsor gains are already flowing.

tone.note: Management was confident on the franchise, historical growth and the SEBI-approved Fund V and Eastgate launches, but declined guidance on carry, deployment, fundraising timing and Fund III outcome; analysts probed the Q1 carry jump, Fund III IRR, AI-sector exposure and valuations.
